en.name: Hildegard of Bingen
en.summary: Twelfth-century German Benedictine abbess, mystic, and polymath, a Doctor of the Church known for visions, music, and writings on medicine.
en.body: Hildegard was given to a monastery as a child and rose to become abbess of her own community at Rupertsberg, where she reported experiencing vivid visions from an early age that she eventually recorded, with Church approval, in an illustrated theological work called Scivias. Remarkably prolific for a woman of her era, she composed a large body of liturgical music still performed today, wrote treatises on natural science and medicine describing the medicinal properties of plants, and corresponded with popes, emperors, and bishops as a respected spiritual authority who did not hesitate to criticize corruption in the Church. She also undertook several preaching tours, unusual for a woman in twelfth-century Europe. She died in 1179, and Pope Benedict XVI formally canonized her and declared her a Doctor of the Church in 2012.
